title: Cement runs short
status: DRAFT for Ilan's review (20 Nov 2026). Not filmed. Plan and decisions: EPISODE_04_PLAN.md (written on its recommended answers). Recording needs the story first: the Main block's cement chain in sample_plan.py made the kit's (LRN-F17). Real data entry only: every chat card is Mesiri's real reply (capture), every website entry filmed step by step (kind "steps", steps-04.cjs, light mode).
source: docs/learning/film/EPISODE_04_PLAN.md (the chain day by day); the starter kit's papers (scripts/learn_kit/make_kit.py: three quotations, Malabar's challan and bill; green_villa.RETURN: return note GV/RN/014); the assistant's tools (apps/whatsapp-assistant/src/agent_api/tools.py: record_transfer, record_receipt on an order, return_to_supplier, count_stock). Construction practice (storing cement, checking at the gate): typical, to be checked by someone who has run sites.
objective: By the end you can walk a material chain across all four people: request, quotations and rate, order, delivery (and a damaged load sent back), stock and use, the supplier's bill checked against order and delivery, payment; and a month-end stock count.

scenes.title: Cement runs short
beats: Monday evening at the Main block. Two bags of cement left, and the conduit work stopped halfway.
Ravi has asked for a hundred bags. By the end of the month, that one line will have passed through four people and eight papers.
Three times on the way, money can quietly leak. This is how it is stopped.

lines.text: One request · four people · eight papers

scenes.title: How a site buys material
beats: Every material on a site is bought the same way, and every step leaves a paper.
The site asks: a request. The office asks the shops for their prices: quotations. It chooses one and orders: a purchase order.
The lorry comes with a challan, what the shop says it sent. The site counts it at the gate, and sends back what is not fit.
Then the shop's bill. Accounts puts it beside the order and the challan, and pays only for what was ordered, at the rate agreed, and what came.

steps.text: The office prices it and orders
Counted at the gate; the bad sent back
Order, delivery and bill side by side, then paid

footer.text: Pay for what was ordered, at the rate agreed, and what came.

scenes.title: Why not just order three hundred bags
beats: Why not ring the usual shop and order everything at once?
Because the usual shop's price is only a price. Three quotations tell you what the price really is, today.
And because cement does not keep. In a damp store it sets in its bag within weeks. A site orders what its store can hold dry, and the rest when there is room.
At the gate, every load is counted, and every bag pressed. A bag that is torn, or hard as a stone, is refused there, before anyone signs for it.

steps.text: Cement goes hard if it waits
Count it, press it, refuse the bad

scenes.title: A hundred bags, or three hundred
beats: Tuesday morning. Ravi's request is the first thing on Anil's Requests page: a hundred bags for the Main block, asked yesterday evening.
Anil looks further than tomorrow. The Main block's plastering starts next week, and the material plan says it needs about three hundred bags this month.
So he asks three suppliers to quote, from Quotations: three hundred bags of cement for the Main block, and two thousand kilos of steel for the Annex's columns.
Malabar, Kerala Steels and Sri Hardwares. Each one is asked the same thing, on the same day.

beats: Quotes take a day. The conduit work cannot wait a day.
Anil rings Ravi: take twenty bags from the Annex, which has enough for this week. Ravi has them carried across, and says so.
Mesiri's card: twenty bags out of the Annex's stock, into the Main block's. One movement, two stocks, neither counted twice.

scenes.title: Three prices, the same day
beats: Wednesday, the quotations come back. This is Malabar's: four hundred rupees a bag of cement, seventy-two a kilo of steel, unloaded at site.
Valid for seven days, GST extra, delivery two days after the order.
Kerala Steels quotes four hundred and twelve and sixty-six. Sri Hardwares, four hundred and eight and seventy.
scenes.note: The kit's quotation says 'For Green Villa, Main block' for both items: it changes to 'Green Villa' (steel for the Annex) with the story (LRN-F17).

scenes.title: Cheapest is not one supplier
beats: Anil puts each supplier's rates in, from their papers.

Mesiri puts them side by side. Cheapest in total is Kerala Steels. But cheapest for cement is Malabar, and for steel, Kerala. Buying each from its cheapest saves three thousand six hundred rupees more.
So Anil orders the cement from Malabar, and the steel from Kerala Steels.
And not three hundred bags: two hundred. That is what the Main block's store can keep dry. The other hundred, when there is room.

scenes.title: Four people, one load of cement
beats: Who does what with these bags?
Ravi asks for them, counts them at the gate, and counts what is left at the month's end.
Anil prices them, orders them, and sends back what is not fit.
Meera checks the bill against the order and the delivery, and pays.
And Ramesh, the owner, sees what is owed, and signs off what the count found.

scenes.title: What the lorry says it brought
beats: Friday, Malabar's lorry is at the Main block's gate. With it, the challan.
Ordered, two hundred. Sent, one hundred and ninety. Ten to follow with the next load.

scenes.title: Counted at the gate
beats: Ravi counts the bags off the lorry: one hundred and ninety. Six of them are torn, and set hard. He puts them aside, on the lorry.
He tells Mesiri what came, and what is wrong with it.
The card puts the hundred and ninety on Malabar's order by itself, and says what the order still has to bring: ten bags.
The six bad bags are for the office to send back. Ravi taps Save.

scenes.title: Sending back what is torn
beats: Anil sends the six bags back, on the same lorry, from Returns: from Friday's delivery, six bags, torn and set hard.
Mesiri writes the return note, and a debit note to Malabar: two thousand four hundred rupees, six bags at the order's rate.
It comes off what we owe Malabar at once, before their bill even arrives. And the six bags leave the Main block's stock: what is left is what is really there.

scenes.title: Ten rupees a bag
beats: Monday, Malabar's bill reaches Meera. One hundred and ninety bags, at four hundred and ten rupees a bag, and GST.
Look again at the rate. The order said four hundred.

scenes.title: The bill beside the order and the delivery
beats: Meera puts the bill in, against Malabar's delivery.

Mesiri puts three things side by side: what was ordered, at four hundred; what came and was kept; and what is billed. The quantity agrees. The rate does not: ten rupees a bag more, one thousand nine hundred rupees before GST.
Nobody would see it on a busy Monday. Mesiri shows it before anyone pays.
Meera rings Malabar. The order's rate was agreed in writing, and Malabar accepts it: the bill is paid at four hundred.

scenes.title: Came, minus used
beats: The plastering has started: fourteen bags a day at the Main block, each one said by Ravi in his evening message.
On Tuesday the ten bags still owed came, and the order is complete.
Stock shows what is left, and how many days it lasts at this week's use. The store has room again, so Anil orders the other hundred bags from Malabar, at the quoted four hundred.
scenes.note: Shot as Anil on day 12, after the second order. Every figure said is read off this screen when it is shot.

scenes.title: Paying the right amount
beats: Saturday, Meera pays Malabar from the Federal Bank account.
Not the bill as it came: the bill at the order's rate, less the debit note for the six bags.
Malabar's page now says what is paid, what is still owed, and against which bill. Nothing is remembered; everything is written.

scenes.title: What is really there
beats: The last day of November. Ravi counts the Main block's store, bag by bag, and says what he finds.
Mesiri compares it with the book: what came, minus what was used, minus what went back. Three bags fewer than the book.
Ravi says why: wastage, spilt and set on the mixing floor. A small, honest difference, and now it is written down.

scenes.title: Paying for what came
beats: What does Ramesh see of all this? Two screens.
Malabar, on Suppliers: the bill, the six bags sent back, the ten rupees a bag not paid, and what is owed now. He did not have to ask anyone.
And the month's count: three bags short at the Main block, wastage, twelve hundred rupees. He approves it, and the book is the store again.
Three leaks this month, each caught by the person whose step it was: at the gate, at the bill, and at the count.

scenes.title: Six ways a load of cement leaks
beats: Six ways a load of cement leaks.
Ordered from the usual shop without a quote: a little more every bag, every month.
Ordered more than the store holds: bags gone hard before they are used.
Signed for two hundred when a hundred and ninety came. And torn bags kept, because sending them back was a bother.
A bill paid as it came, ten rupees above the order. And a store never counted, so nobody knows what is missing until the job is over.

scenes.title: Three questions
beats: Three questions. Pause, and answer them before you go on.
One: why did Anil order two hundred bags when the month needs three hundred? Because the store can keep two hundred dry. Cement that waits goes hard.
Two: what three things does Meera put side by side before she pays? The order, the delivery, and the bill.
Three: who sends the torn bags back, and what does it change? Anil, from Returns. The debit note takes them off what we owe Malabar at once, and off the stock.
Next: wages week. Ravi's attendance becomes Saturday's wages. Now play the material chain yourself: chapters five and eight of the guided project.
